lead: Snap / SNAP — the survivor of the Facebook crash
smaller: Peloton Interactive / PTON — the takeover lottery ticket
Ford Motor / F — the EV dream at a discount
MicroStrategy / MSTR — Saylor's leveraged ticket on the crypto bounce
why_lead: Snap was the largest one-session mover on the card (38.91 USD, +58.82% on 2022-02-04; +27.91% over five sessions) and had explicit retail-attention evidence: a Moomoo item framing it as a 50% one-day jackpot [[n0876]] and The Ankler's 'pops 60%' [[n0815]], plus Barron's 'best day ever' [[n0817]] and TechCrunch [[n1121]]. The story is simple and repeatable (the survivor of the Meta crash [[n0658]], [[n0540]], [[n1102]]) and the 4 February session is new relative to anything a 4 February edition could have known. No strictly earlier retail notes or drafts existed when this date was first selected; the parallel 1–4 February drafts written since (GameStop; Alphabet; Meta on 3 and 4 February; Amazon and Bitcoin as 4 February secondaries) do not include Snap, and Meta is kept only as the foil because its crash was the 2022-02-03/04 lead and its 4 February move was only -0.28%. The Snap surge itself is a completed 4 February session, unavailable to the 4 February edition.
why_smaller: Peloton: takeover-lottery narrative distinct from the earnings gap — WSJ exclusive on Amazon and other suitors [[n0770]], Guardian [[n0745]], CNBC surge report [[n0803]], Bloomberg regulatory-headache caveat [[n0866]]; card shows a beaten stock (24.60 USD, -27.35% over 20 sessions) with only +1.44% in the completed 4 February session.

Ford Motor: the buy-the-EV-dip narrative — the largest US single-stock decline on the card for 4 February (17.96 USD, -9.70%; -26.57% over 20 sessions), 'skid despite a bullish 2022 outlook' [[n0661]], up to $20 billion EV investment [[n0542]], EV sales boom [[n1143]]; breaks on chip-driven production cuts [[n1160]], [[n1134]] and the Rivian-mark-inflated profit [[n0660]]. Not used in any earlier retail note or draft (2022-02-01 to 02-04).

MicroStrategy: the leveraged crypto-rebound narrative — Bitcoin back past $40,000 [[n0945]] (a 4 February-stamped report, newer than the strictly earlier 2022-02-04 draft whose Bitcoin item covered only bitcoin holding steady on 3 February), BTC 42,412.43 USD (+9.47% over five days), MSTR +15.16%, GBTC +13.52%, RIOT +12.04%; Saylor [[n0510]] and Fundstrat [[n0947]] for the faith, the $320 million hack [[n0923]] and the UN report on North Korea's stolen-crypto funding [[n1413]] for the break (replacing the India 30% tax, already a break test in the 2022-02-02 Solana item, with newer evidence).
considered_not_chosen: Amazon / AMZN (+13.54%, record $190 billion value gain [[n0747]]): originally drafted as a secondary item, but replaced because the strictly earlier 2022-02-04 draft already ran Amazon on the same results evidence (AWS, Rivian gain, Prime fee, AWS-only operating profit); the completed session alone did not justify another item.

Meta Platforms / FB dip-buying (-21.42% over five sessions, [[n0684]], [[n0736]]): the crash itself was the 3 February session and is earlier-edition material; used as the foil in the Snap lead instead.
Pinterest / PINS (+11.18%, [[n0703]]): same results-day relief narrative as Snap, so folded into the lead rather than given its own slot.
Digital World Acquisition / DWAC (+22.84% over five sessions, +40.12% over 20): large move but no own-date DWAC headline to explain it.
PayPal / PYPL (-22.90% over five sessions, [[n0580]]): worst-ever day was 2 February, earlier-edition material with no new catalyst.
Unity Software / U (+17.42%) and AppLovin / APP (+12.38%): large moves without own-date catalyst or attention headlines.

GameStop/AMC anniversary coverage ([[n0849]], [[n0496]], [[n0436]]): used as the historical analog rather than as a trade, since GME (-21.90%) and AMC (-31.66%) over 20 sessions show no fresh catalyst.
